# Data Source Plan

Working document for choosing the data sources behind the counterparty pre-check. Start with candidates, verify each one, and end with a final list the connectors are built from.

## How we decide

Each candidate is scored on the same fields before it goes on the final list:

- **Covers:** which entity types (company, LLP, proprietor) and which fields
- **Key:** what it is looked up by (CIN, GSTIN, PAN, name, city)
- **Access:** free, key-based, paid, captcha-gated, or no public route
- **Terms:** whether automated use is allowed, and at what volume
- **Verified:** seen working in a live call or a documented schema, or only from search results
- **Decision:** keep, fixture-only, or drop

A source only goes on the final list when it is verified and its terms allow our use. Otherwise it stays a fixture or is dropped.

## Part 1: Quantitative KYC

Structured records about the entity: identity, registration, status and tax numbers. These are the facts the identifier checks and resolver depend on.

| Source | Provider | Covers | Key | Access | Terms | Verified | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identifier format and checksum (PAN, GSTIN, CIN) | Offline, our own logic | All | Identifier | None | n/a | To build and test | Keep |
| MCA company master | Sandbox.co.in aggregator (`POST /kyc/mca/company/master-data`) | Companies, LLP unclear | CIN | Aggregator key | Aggregator terms | Schema read from docs, no live call | Candidate |
| MCA company master | MCA on API Setu (partner listed) | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Not found in catalogue | Check partners portal |
| MCA name lookup | None found | n/a | Name | n/a | n/a | No | Gap |
| GST taxpayer status | GSTN (partner listed on API Setu) | Unknown | GSTIN | Unknown | Unknown | Not found in catalogue | Check partners portal |
| GST taxpayer status | Third-party providers (e.g. Sandbox, Masters India, Eko, Deepvue) | Businesses with GSTIN | GSTIN | Paid, some free lookups | Provider terms | Search results only | Candidate |
| PAN verification | Third-party vendors | Individuals and businesses | PAN | Paid | Provider terms | Search results only | Candidate, optional |
| IBBI insolvency announcements | ibbi.gov.in public site | Companies under insolvency | CIN | Public website | Site terms, check caching | Keyed pages seen in search | Candidate |
| Crustdata company data | Crustdata | Companies | Name or domain | 5,000 credits for participants | Provider terms | Not tested | Test on 5 entities |
| data.gov.in company master | data.gov.in | About 3.67M companies | CIN or name | Not an accessible API (per our check) | Open data licence | No API found | Drop unless a route appears |

### Open quantitative checks

- [ ] Browse the API Setu directory for MCA, GSTN, company, CIN, IBBI and PAN APIs (the directory is JavaScript-rendered, so use a browser)
- [ ] Check the API Setu partners portal for MCA and GSTN onboarding
- [ ] Confirm whether the Sandbox MCA endpoint returns LLPs
- [ ] Get a GST route with a verified live call, and record its free lookup limit
- [ ] Record each chosen source's rate limit, from its own directory or docs page

## Part 2: Qualitative KYC

Information about the entity's conduct and reputation that is not in a registry. This is where the agent finds what a quick search misses, so every claim here needs a cited link.

| Source type | Example sources | Covers | Key | Access | Terms | Verified | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Adverse media | Web search tool, news sites | Companies and individuals named in news | Name plus city | Search tool | Per site | Not tested | Candidate, lowest confidence |
| Court and litigation records | eCourts (captcha-gated, no open API verified) | Companies and parties | Name or case number | Captcha | Not allowed to automate captcha | No | Roadmap only |
| Insolvency and enforcement notices | IBBI, other regulator notices | Companies, LLPs | CIN | Public site | Site terms | Keyed pages seen | Candidate |
| Regulator actions and defaulter lists | RBI, SEBI, other public notices | Companies, individuals | Name | Public site | Site terms | Not checked | To explore |
| Company filings and charges | MCA filings, charge registrations | Companies | CIN | Portal access | Portal terms | Not checked | To explore |
| Reviews and public reputation | Google reviews, Justdial, IndiaMART | Businesses | Name plus city | Public site | Site terms | Not checked | To explore, may drop |

### Open qualitative checks

- [ ] Test adverse media on 5 known entities, and check how many results link to the right entity
- [ ] Confirm which regulator and enforcement notices are public and cacheable
- [ ] Decide whether reviews are in scope, since they carry bias and legal risk
- [ ] Write the query templates for adverse media and record the result count per entity

## Final list

Filled in once Parts 1 and 2 are verified. Each entry is a connector the pipeline calls.

| # | Source | Type | Key | Mode (live, cached or fixture) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | To be decided | — | — | — | — |

## Notes

- API Setu's terms apply only to APIs published on API Setu. Third-party aggregators have their own terms, so each source is recorded with its own terms.
- Demo data comes from fixtures or cached snapshots, and the report must say so.
- Proprietors have no MCA record, so they rely on GST, identifier checks and media only. The report marks that lower confidence.

| # | SOP check | No NOC | With NOC |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MCA: company name, status, age, registered address, class, capital (needs CIN) | Yes | Yes |
| 2 | MCA: directors | No, excluded by our plan | Likely, verify endpoint and terms |

| 7 | PAN: format, checksum, entity type | Yes, offline | Yes |
| 8 | PAN: name and number match against government record | No, the IT portal is captcha-gated | Yes, via a paid PAN vendor |
| 9 | PAN: address | No | Unknown |
| 10 | Utility bill: readable, dated within 2 months, name matches | Yes, if the bill is uploaded | Yes |
| 11 | Utility bill address vs master and GST address | Yes | Yes |
| 12 | Issues of concern: IBBI insolvency by CIN | Yes | Yes |
| 13 | Issues of concern: adverse media | Partial, low confidence | Partial |
| 14 | Director identity KYC (ID, photo, Aadhaar) | No, out of scope | Only via a licensed identity vendor with the director's own consent, not in our plan |
| 15 | Director background or defaulter checks | No, plan excludes personal dossiers | No |
| 16 | Collecting documents from forwarder and shipper | No, operational step | No |
| 17 | HO OK / NOT OK decision within 30 minutes | Partial, see below | Partial, with more checks passing |

**Tally**

- **No NOC:** 5 yes, 4 partial, 1 unknown, 7 no (17 steps). The agent can check company status and identity, read the utility bill, and report the IBBI status, but cannot confirm directors, PAN name match, or GST details without a verified provider.
- **With NOC:** 9 yes (directors pending verification), 3 partial, 2 unknown, 3 no. The NOC unlocks the PAN name match and the GST and directors data, but director identity KYC and background checks remain outside our scope.

**Gaps that matter**

- **PAN name match is the most important check** in the SOP for catching fraud, and it is the one we cannot do without consent.
- **Name-only intake fails.** Steps 1 and 12 need a CIN, so the counterparty must supply it or we need a name-to-CIN source.
- **The SOP's OK / NOT OK verdict conflicts with our plan's "no verdicts" rule.** The agent can produce a per-check pass, fail or unverified report and a list of missing documents for a human to decide, but it should not issue the OK itself.
- **The diagram's centre is director KYC**, and our plan excludes it. If the business needs it, that is a scope change, not a data-source change.

# Data Source Plan

Working document for the counterparty pre-check. It maps each check the agent runs to a candidate source, then ends in a final connector list. The checks follow the flow in the KYC SOP we reviewed (`sample_SMB_KYC.pdf`), with the steps the agent cannot do left out.

## How we decide

Each candidate is scored on the same fields before it goes on the final list:

- **Covers:** entity types (company, LLP, proprietor) and fields returned
- **Key:** what it is looked up by (CIN, GSTIN, PAN, name, city)
- **Needs NOC:** whether the counterparty's consent is required before the lookup
- **Terms:** whether automated use is allowed, and at what volume
- **Verified:** seen in a live call or a documented schema, or only in search results
- **Decision:** keep, fixture-only, or drop

A source goes on the final list only when it is verified and its terms allow our use. Otherwise it stays a fixture or is dropped.

## Flow

```
1. Intake            name, CIN / GSTIN / PAN / city, entity type
2. Identifier checks offline: format, checksum, PAN entity type
3. Quantitative      registry and tax facts (Q1 to Q6)
4. Qualitative       insolvency, media, notices, proprietor background (L1 to L4)
5. Reconcile         rank sources, mark each check pass / flag / unverified
6. Report            per-check status, evidence links, missing items
```

Steps 3 and 4 run in parallel. A failed connector is marked unverified and lowers the report's confidence.

## Step 2: Identifier checks (offline)

| ID | Check | Source | Key | Needs NOC | Verified | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | PAN, GSTIN and CIN format and checksum | Our own logic | Identifier | No | To build and test | Keep |
| I2 | PAN entity type against claimed entity type | Our own logic (PAN fourth character) | PAN | No | To build and test | Keep |

## Step 3: Quantitative checks (registry and tax facts)

| ID | Check | Candidate source | Key | Needs NOC | Verified | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | MCA master: status, age, registered address, class, capital, industry code | Sandbox.co.in MCA endpoint (`POST /kyc/mca/company/master-data`) | CIN | No | Schema read from docs, no live call | Candidate |
| Q1a | MCA master via API Setu | MCA is a listed API Setu partner | CIN | No | Not found in catalogue | Check partners portal |
| Q2 | Directors (names, designations) | Sandbox MCA directors endpoint, seen in a community Postman example | CIN | Yes | Not verified | Candidate, confirm terms |
| Q3 | GST status, legal and trade name, registered address, active since | Third-party GST providers (Sandbox, Masters India, Eko, Deepvue); GSTN via API Setu if a route is confirmed | GSTIN | No, verify per provider | Search results only | Candidate |
| Q4 | GST SAC codes | Same GST provider, field not confirmed | GSTIN | No, verify per provider | Not verified | Keep only if the provider returns it |
| Q5 | PAN name match against government record | PAN verification vendors | PAN | Yes | Search results only | Candidate |
| Q6 | Utility bill: dated within 2 months, name matches, address matches master and GST | Counterparty upload, read by OCR | Upload | No, the counterparty supplies it | To build | Keep |

## Step 4: Qualitative checks (conduct and reputation)

Every claim here needs a cited link. Qualitative results carry lower confidence than registry facts.

| ID | Check | Candidate source | Key | Needs NOC | Verified | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Insolvency and liquidation announcements | ibbi.gov.in public announcements | CIN | No | Keyed pages seen in search | Candidate, check terms and caching |
| L2 | Adverse media | Web search tool, news sites | Name plus city | No | Not tested | Candidate, lowest confidence |
| L3 | Regulator and defaulter notices | RBI, SEBI and other public notices | Name | No | Not checked | To explore |
| L4 | Proprietor background (business-linked signals only) | Web search and news, scoped to the business | Owner name plus business name or GSTIN | Open, see below | Not built | Proposed |
| L5 | Litigation | eCourts | Name or case number | Not applicable | Captcha-gated, no open API | Roadmap only |
| L6 | Charges and filings | MCA filings | CIN | Not applicable | Portal access not checked | To explore |
| L7 | Reviews and public reputation | Google, Justdial, IndiaMART | Name plus city | No | Not checked | May drop, bias and legal risk |

### L4: Proprietor background (proposed design)

A proprietor has no MCA record, and the owner's conduct is often the main risk. The check looks for public signals that concern the owner's role in the business, and nothing about the person's private life.

**In scope**

- Public news or reports naming the owner together with the business name, trade name or GSTIN
- Regulator or enforcement notices naming the owner in their business role
- Public business listings or the business's own website describing the owner's role

**Out of scope**

- Family members, home address, personal phone numbers
- Personal social media accounts and photographs
- Data from brokers, leaks or scraped contact databases
- Anything that cannot be tied to the business
- Any identity-document or biometric check

**Attribution rule**

A signal is attached to the owner only when two identifiers match, such as owner name plus business name, or owner name plus city plus trade name. Otherwise the signal is reported as "cannot attribute", not dropped silently.

**Storage**

Keep the cited snippet, URL and retrieval date. Do not build a standing profile. Apply `CACHE_TTL_HOURS` to these records, and delete them on expiry.

**Output**

A separate "Proprietor background" section in the report. An empty result means "no public signal found in the sources checked", never "clean". The report states which sources were searched.

**Demo**

Synthetic proprietors only, as the plan already requires.

**Decisions needed before the hour-3 gate**

- Does the proprietor consent before the run, or only get notified?
- Which signal types are in: news, regulator notices, business listings, or only some?
- Legal basis under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023: needs review with counsel, not decided here.

## Step 5 and 6: Reconcile and report

| ID | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Per-check status: pass, flag or unverified, with evidence links | Replaces the SOP's single OK / NOT OK at the agent level |
| R2 | Missing-items list for the human reviewer | Names the document or check still needed |
| R3 | Confidence per section | Lower where a source failed or a check is unverified |

The agent does not issue a verdict. The SOP's OK or NOT OK stays a human decision, made from R1 to R3.

## Dropped SOP checks

These steps from the SOP are not in the agent's scope, whatever consent is in place.

| SOP step | Why it is dropped |
|---|---|
| Director identity KYC (ID document, photo, Aadhaar) | Needs an identity vendor and the director's own consent, and is outside the pre-check |
| PAN address match | Typical PAN name-match checks do not return an address, and no source was found |
| Collecting documents from forwarder and shipper | Operational work done by people, not the agent |
| MCA name lookup | No name route found. Intake needs a CIN until one is found, so this is a dependency, not a step |

## Open quantitative checks

- [ ] Browse the API Setu directory for MCA, GSTN, company, CIN, IBBI and PAN APIs (JavaScript-rendered, use a browser)
- [ ] Check the API Setu partners portal for MCA and GSTN onboarding
- [ ] Confirm whether the Sandbox MCA endpoint returns LLPs
- [ ] Confirm whether the Sandbox directors endpoint exists and what its terms allow
- [ ] Get a GST route with a verified live call, record its free lookup limit, and check whether SAC codes are returned
- [ ] Record each chosen source's rate limit from its own docs page

## Open qualitative checks

- [ ] Test adverse media on 5 known entities and count results that link to the right entity
- [ ] Confirm which regulator and enforcement notices are public and cacheable
- [ ] Decide the L4 consent flow and signal types, then test attribution on 5 synthetic owners
- [ ] Decide whether reviews (L7) are in scope
- [ ] Write the query templates for L2 and L4

## Final list

Filled in once the checks above are verified. Each entry is a connector the pipeline calls.

| # | Check | Source | Key | Mode (live, cached or fixture) | Needs NOC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | To be decided | — | — | — | — |

## Notes

- API Setu's terms apply only to APIs published on API Setu. Third-party aggregators have their own terms, recorded per source.
- Demo data comes from fixtures or cached snapshots, and the report says so.
- Proprietors have no MCA record, so they rely on Q3, I1 and I2, Q6, L1 to L4 and the report marks that lower confidence.

Web search itself has two limits. It returns indexed pages rather than live records, and the pages that show up are mostly third-party sites like [expressgst.com](https://www.expressgst.com/gst-number-search/) or guides that describe how to look things up. Those sites are not authoritative, and their terms are unknown.

Routes that stay inside our rules:

1. **Document ingest (no NOC needed for the agent's logic).** The counterparty supplies the official printouts the SOP already asks for: MCA master data, GST registration certificate and PAN card. The agent reads them with OCR and checks them against each other. This covers the SOP's document steps directly.
2. **Licensed aggregators.** Sandbox, Masters India and similar providers have licensed access to these records, so the captcha is not our problem. This is the realistic live route, at a cost. It is also where the NOC matters for PAN name match.
3. **Human-in-the-loop lookup.** The SOP's operator runs the government search and pastes the result into the agent. The agent then does the reconciliation and the qualitative work. This matches how the SOP already runs.
4. **Web search for qualitative signals.** This works for open pages such as IBBI announcements, news, and regulator notices, as long as their terms allow it. I could not fetch the IBBI page in this session, so that still needs checking.

For proprietors, the PAN is an individual's, so the registry checks depend more on the counterparty's own documents than on any database.

For the hackathon, I'd suggest: Sandbox for MCA and GST with fixtures as the fallback, document ingest for the SOP's documents, and web search for L2 and L3. No, Sandbox does not solve the problem on its own. It covers one check: MCA company status and identity by CIN. It leaves out GST, PAN name match, directors, LLPs, proprietors, and every qualitative check.

Crustdata and cfo.ai are not interchangeable with it:

- **cfo.ai is not a data source.** The hackathon requires it for the business plan (pricing, costs, runway), so it stays in that role either way.
- **Crustdata is a B2B enrichment API.** It advertises [60M+ companies and 1B+ people](https://crustdata.com/) with firmographic and people data, aimed at sales and AI agents. It is not a registry or KYC source, so it returns no GST, PAN, CIN or insolvency records. Its India coverage of small businesses is unverified, and the plan already marks it as a drop-if-thin test. If we used its people data for proprietors, that would raise the same personal-data questions as the dossier design.

On a US pivot, the same two-part shape works, but the sources differ:

| Check | Likely US sources | Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Entity registration and status | State Secretary of State registries; [OpenCorporates](https://apify.com/ryanclinton/opencorporates-search) for aggregation | Each state has its own site and format. OpenCorporates' US coverage needs a paid key. |
| Public company filings | [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/) | Covers public filers only, so it misses most SMBs. Check its developer rules. |
| Sanctions | [OFAC SDN list](https://www.opensanctions.org/datasets/us_sanctions/) via OpenSanctions, or [moov-io/ofac](https://github.com/moov-io/ofac) | Free to download and match against. This is a strong, low-risk qualitative check. |
| Litigation and bankruptcy | PACER (paid) or CourtListener | Not verified in this session. |
| Adverse media | Web search, as in the India plan | Same confidence limits. |

**My recommendation:** keep India for the hackathon. Sandbox covers the MCA and GST backbone. The gaps (PAN name match, proprietors, document checks) are real, but the existing plan already handles them with fixtures, NOC-gated lookups and the document route. A US pivot means rewriting the research, the test list and the demo, with about 36 hours left.
